learn.title: Name the result
learn.body: A prompt should make the intended result clear. A topic tells the model what to discuss; a goal tells it what to produce for you. Start with one objective so the response has a clear job.

learn.title: Task and outcome
learn.body: Write about habits names a topic. Draft a 100-word welcome message for a new habit tracker names a task and a usable outcome. The second request gives the model a finish line without pretending the wording guarantees a perfect answer.

learn.title: Keep one main objective
learn.body: A request to design a screen, write its code, and plan a launch mixes different outcomes. Split unrelated goals into separate requests. A single goal can still have several requirements, such as a length and an audience.

learn.title: From vague to useful
learn.body: Turn a broad habit-tracker request into one clear objective.
steps: Weak start: Help with my habit app.
Choose the task: draft the welcome message.
Name the outcome: one message of at most 60 words.
Final goal: Draft one welcoming message of at most 60 words for someone starting a personal habit tracker.

learn.title: Check before sending
learn.body: Ask whether you could recognize a useful response without interpreting several competing requests. If the goal is still improve everything or make it better, choose the particular result you want first.

learn.title: You choose the objective
learn.body: The model can help phrase a goal, but it cannot know which result matters to you unless you decide. Choosing between a name, a message, and a plan is product judgment. Clear prompting starts with that human choice.
A clear goal guides the response; it does not remove the need to review what comes back.

questions.prompt: Which request has the clearest goal?
choices: Write three names for a habit tracker
questions.explanation: It names one task, writing names, and a concrete outcome, three names. The other requests leave the intended result unclear.

questions.prompt: A useful prompt begins with one clear \_\_.
questions.explanation: One clear objective tells the model what the response should accomplish. Extra conversation or politeness cannot replace that direction.

questions.prompt: Complete the advice with one word: A goal names the intended ___.
questions.explanation: The intended outcome or result is what you want to receive, such as a 60-word welcome message.

questions.prompt: Match each vague topic to a focused goal.
pairs: Suggest five names for a reading habit
List three labels for the check-in screen
questions.explanation: Each focused goal names a particular deliverable and amount, rather than asking for general discussion.

questions.prompt: Put this prompt revision in a sensible order.
steps: Notice that Help with my tracker has no clear result
Choose one task, such as drafting a welcome message
Specify the desired outcome, including its length
Review whether the request still has one main objective
questions.explanation: First identify the gap, then choose the task and outcome. A final check catches competing objectives before you send the prompt.

questions.prompt: You need both a privacy summary and five reminder messages. What best preserves one clear objective per prompt?
choices: Ask for both in one request with no priorities
Start two separate requests, one for each deliverable
Replace both goals with Improve my app
Ask only which goal the model prefers
questions.explanation: The deliverables are unrelated, so separate requests keep each objective clear. The model should not choose your product goal for you.
